newsitem.title: USA: ABC/Money consumer comfort index down in Oct 6 wk.
newsitem.headline: ABC/Money consumer comfort index down in Oct 6 wk.

text.p: The Money Magazine/ABC News consumer comfort index fell one point to -6 in the week ended October 6, but remained well above its 12-month average of -13 and within four points of its all-time high reached in 1987.
"Bolstering the index was a continued upbeat attitude among women," the report said.

The survey, this time with 1,044 respondents, polls consumers nationwide about the national economy, their own finances and their willingness to spend money. The poll has a margin of error of plus/minus 3.5 percent.
Respondents' confidence in the economy held unchanged at its six-year-high level of -16.
Confidence in personal finances remained at 20, while Americans' rating of buying climate dipped to -22 from -20 the previous week.
Regionally, confidence fell in the Northeast for the first time in seven years, but the index hit an 11-week high of -11 in the West.
